newsitem.title: USA: Meeting with Clinton on budget positive - Gingrich.
newsitem.headline: Meeting with Clinton on budget positive - Gingrich.

text.p: House of Representatives Speaker Newt Gingrich told reporters that a meeting of the bipartisan congressional leadership with U.S. President Bill Clinton on Tuesday had been "very, very positive."
Gingrich, who left the White House meeting early, said the legislators and the president had had a good conversation on implementing the balanced budget agreement reached on May 2.

"We are working on getting the balanced budget agreement and the tax cut agreement through the House today and through the Senate and through conference this week," Gingrich told reporters. "There was a very positive spirit of cooperation."

Gingrich said the two sides also sought to find common ground on the question of ensuring that the federal government remains open while the Congress works to pass the legislation needed to put the balanced budget agreement into law.
"We're trying to find some common ground that would be basically a commitment to keep it open, whether that's signing the continuing resolution or by some other device," he said.

Republicans are seeking to tie a disaster relief bill to an unrelated provision that would automatically keep the government running next year, albeit at lower spending levels than in the current fiscal year, if Congress and the White House fail to agree on the spending bills that put the budget into practice.
House Minority Leader Dick Gephardt, who according to a top Democratic aide is expected to vote against the balanced budget plan, left the White House by a side door, declining to speak to reporters.
